audit.whatIsWrong: The content chart is Lucian, Lucian, Lucian, Skill, Lucian, Skill, Lucian — Lucian owns five of seven stages in a matchup Malphite wins 55.71% over 3177 games, the largest sample in the file. The full layer's chart for the same matchup is Skill, Lucian, Skill, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite, and the content whys agree with the full layer, not with the content chart.
audit.why: The two layers of the same page contradict each other on four stages, and the losing side is credited with the whole late game. whys[3] says Malphite 'starts out-trading his all-AD damage', whys[5] says 'you out-trade and out-durable him here', whys[6] says nothing lets him reclaim it — every one of those stages is marked Lucian or Skill on the chart above them.
audit.corrected: Content chart aligned to the full layer and to its own whys: Skill, Lucian, Skill, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seismic Shard and Ground Slam both ground. Relentless Pursuit is Lucian's only dash and his only disengage. No string says grounding exists.
audit.why: The entry's level-6 plan is 'he cannot dash out of an R that's already on top of him', which relies on landing a 1000-range ult before he reacts. Grounding makes the same play deterministic: a 7s Ground Slam removes the dash first, and then Unstoppable Force is not a race. That is the difference between a coin-flip engage and a repeatable one.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam grounds Relentless Pursuit — slam on his step-up, then commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere', sequencingCues 0. Nowhere does the entry give a number, and the one number that matters is conditional. Riot on Relentless Pursuit: 'Lightslinger attacks reduce Relentless Pursuit's cooldown.'
audit.why: A reader who counts 16 seconds off his dash and steps up on 16 will die, because every double-shot he lands on you or the wave has been shortening it the whole time. Telling someone the base number without the reduction clause is worse than telling them nothing. Piercing Light is 9s down to 5s and The Culling is 110/100/90 against your 130/115/100.
audit.corrected: Relentless Pursuit reads 16s but Lightslinger attacks cut it, so it returns earlier than the tooltip.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lucian.json (E Relentless Pursuit 16/15.5/15/14.5/14, P Lightslinger, Q 9/8/7/6/5, R 110/100/90)

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'never names any of Lucian's abilities'. The entry says 'double-shot passive', 'Q-W poke', 'his E dash', 'his Culling range' — only the ult is close to named.
audit.why: The passive is Lightslinger and it is what makes every ability cast into two attacks, which is the actual reason his poke chunks. Naming it also makes the cooldown-reduction clause on his dash comprehensible, because the two are the same mechanic.
audit.corrected: Lightslinger, Piercing Light and Relentless Pursuit named in the strings that describe them.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lucian.json (P Lightslinger, Q Piercing Light, E Relentless Pursuit)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] credits the level-6 flip to a point-blank R 'through his Culling range', with no mechanism for why he cannot leave.
audit.why: The mechanism exists and is better than the one given. Grounding is what removes his exit; the R only has to land after that.
audit.corrected: Level-6 spike restated as Ground Slam grounding the dash, then Unstoppable Force.

edits.before: This is where it turns. Once Thunderclap (W) gives you armor and empowered autos, and Ground Slam (E) lands its attack-speed slow, his double-shot DPS and kiting damage fall off hard — E is a direct counter to an auto-attack ADC. The real flip is level 6: walk him down behind Granite Shield, and when he commits his E to reposition, fire Unstoppable Force point-blank for the knock-up. He cannot dash out of an R that's already on top of him, and a Q slow into R erases his ability to kite. That's your kill window.
edits.after: This is where it turns. Once Thunderclap (W) gives you armor and empowered autos, and Ground Slam (E) lands its attack-speed cut, his Lightslinger double-shots fall off hard — E is a direct counter to an auto-attack ADC. The real flip is level 6, and it is not a race: Ground Slam grounds Relentless Pursuit, so slam on his step-up, take the dash off him, then fire Unstoppable Force point-blank. Do not count a flat 16s on that dash — every Lightslinger attack he lands shortens it, so it comes back sooner than the tooltip reads.

notes: Biggest single fix here is structural: the content chart handed Lucian five of seven stages in Malphite's best-sampled winning matchup (55.71% over 3177 games), while the full layer for the same matchup and the content whys directly beneath the chart both say the opposite from level 4 onward. Content chart is now aligned to the full layer. Mechanically, Ground Slam's grounding against Relentless Pursuit was absent everywhere and it converts the level-6 all-in from a timing race into a two-button sequence. The cooldown nuance worth more than the base number: Lightslinger attacks reduce Relentless Pursuit, so 16s is a ceiling he almost never pays. Not asserted: whether Seismic Shard, a projectile, can be intercepted by anything in his kit — nothing in it blocks projectiles.
